title: Forced full re-prefill audit of multi-turn tool workflows
cohort: read-only log audit; no engine was started, stopped or loaded

server_logs.verbosity: Most logs use -lv 4, which prints the common prefix ('checking sim (lcp/new)'), checkpoint restores, forced re-processing and reused tokens. Verbosity-3 logs (14-15 October, early Flint smokes) contribute client timings only.

excluded: local-data/2026-11-03-campaign (live Groot benchmark on port 8081): not analysed
Strata and azllm engines: client timings only, no llama.cpp server log
benchmarks/2026-10-13-instructions/*.stderr.log for 13-14 October private runs: outside the audited log paths; those three runs are classified from client timings
scope.privacy:
Numbers only. No prompt, answer, file or editor text was copied. Whitespace-only features (for example a trailing '


') were computed for the boundary analysis.

method.continuation_turn: A request with index >= 1 inside one benchmark conversation (scenario directory or private run).
method.ideal_reuse: min(previous KV tokens, current prompt tokens - 1). Previous KV = the server's 'stop processing: n_tokens' for the previous task, or prompt_n + cache_n + predicted_n - 1 when unmatched.
method.lost_tokens: ideal_reuse - cache_n, split with the server LCP into history_mismatch_tokens (cached tokens after the point where the re-rendered history first differs) and checkpoint_rollback_tokens (identical prefix tokens re-processed because the recurrent or sliding-window state could not be rolled back to the LCP).
method.lost_seconds: Interpolated from the task's own 'prompt processing, n_tokens, t' progress lines over the first lost tokens; average ms/token when no progress lines exist.
method.matching: Client turns were joined to server tasks by (prompt_n, predicted_n, cache_n) and time; 762 of 805 timed turns matched.
method.limits: LCP is the server's token-level common prefix with its cached slot, not with older states. Mismatch tokens include intended template changes (for example dropped reasoning), so they are an upper bound on what a lossless round trip would save.

headline.verdict: Forced full re-processing inside a tool loop happened once in 561 continuation turns (Gemma-4-31B, 9,778 tokens, 512.7 s). For Qwen3.6 it never happened: 222 of 224 continuation turns reused the whole previous KV including the generated reasoning, and the two partial turns lost 19.4 s in total. The 700-860 s private-audit times are new tool-result prefill and decode, not re-prefill. Most of the 1,097 s lost across all models is Gemma-4: one turn whose template dropped earlier reasoning (512.7 s) and 65 short-context sliding-window restores that re-processed already cached output (341 s with Flint). The large avoidable re-prefills are in real editor traffic, where shared-prefix requests diverged before every retained checkpoint (578 s in four requests).

boundary_whitespace_vs_divergence.definition: Previous output flagged when reasoning_content has leading whitespace or trailing whitespace other than one newline, or content has leading/trailing whitespace.
boundary_whitespace_vs_divergence.qwen36_reading: Qwen3.6: 222 clean outputs re-rendered identically; the one output whose reasoning ended with three newlines diverged (template trims reasoning before '\n</think>'); one clean private output diverged 34 tokens into its reasoning (cause not visible at -lv 4; non-canonical tokenization is a plausible, unverified explanation).

server_log_lines.reading: Most 'forcing full prompt re-processing' lines are benign: 54 of the 57 lines on a new case's first request share only 1-90 tokens with the previous case; three share 297-349 tokens (identical first prompts with no checkpoint that early). Only one line falls on a continuation turn. 'erased invalidated context checkpoint' is housekeeping after any divergence, not a re-prefill by itself.

cross_case_first_turns.note: Benchmark artifact: a new case can partly reuse the previous case's checkpoints, so first-turn prefill varies (0-370 tokens). It is small except on the slow Flint low-residency profile (103-114 s). Each case's deadline includes it.

iswa_short_context_rollbacks.criterion: Previous KV no larger than the SWA cache (Gemma-4 1,280 cells, Flint 768), so the SWA cache provably still held every position, and more than 4 identical tokens were re-processed.
iswa_short_context_rollbacks.mechanism: pos_min_thold = max(0, pos_next - n_swa) clamps to 0 below the window and the SWA cache's pos_min is 0, so the restore test is true even for an exact prefix match; the newest checkpoint (5 tokens before the previous prompt end) is restored and the previous output is re-processed. Example: Flint task with LCP 283 = every cached token restored a checkpoint at 250. This reads as an unnecessary restore in b11562; it was not checked against later builds.

gemma_tool_call_tail_mismatch.reading: Every Gemma-4 tool-call turn re-renders its final 17-26 tokens (the thought/tool-call boundary) differently from what was generated. Cost is about 0.2-1.4 s per turn; the exact tokens need LLAMA_SERVER_SLOTS_DEBUG to identify.

lab_requests_without_client_records.note: Context-growth probes and Gemma-31B calibration requests; they are synthetic prompts, not tool workflows, and are excluded from the workflow totals.

events.pattern: cold re-send after native idle sleep
events.note: Sleep frees weights and KV; the editor resends the full history. Not a cache-reuse defect. Two further cold first prompts at server start (11,810 and 25,200 tokens; 80.0 and 377.8 s) are excluded from every waste total.

editor_production_logs.reading: Editor clients (Copilot/Continue) share an 11.5K-12.6K-token system and tool prefix. Four requests diverged 600-5,800 tokens before the previous prompt end, or right after that prefix, while the server held only end-of-conversation checkpoints, so 11.5K-19.4K identical tokens were re-processed each time. In the 18 October case the boundary checkpoints (11,478 and 11,533) had existed and were evicted by the 4-checkpoint limit; in the other three no checkpoint was ever created at or before the divergence. One further request probably returned to a conversation displaced by an interleaved chat (single slot, --cache-ram 0).

causes.source: b11562 tools/server/server-context.cpp:3596 (n_past = common prefix with cached tokens, including generated ones), :3679-3777 (restore the newest checkpoint below the divergence or force n_past = 0), :3981-4067 (checkpoints only while processing a prompt: at user-message starts and 4 + n_ubatch and 4 tokens before the prompt end), :2526-2556 (when full, evict checkpoints within checkpoint_min_step of an earlier one, then the oldest); common/common.h:637-639 (32 checkpoints, 8192 spacing by default; our Qwen profiles pass --ctx-checkpoints 4).
causes.effect: The recurrent state exists only at the end of the cached sequence. Any divergence inside the previous assistant output rolls back to 4 tokens before the previous prompt end and re-processes the whole previous output; a divergence earlier than every retained checkpoint forces a full re-prefill.

causes.applies_to: Qwen3.5+ templates (issue #30357; PR #30557 in b11951 is partial)
causes.source:
Qwen3.6 template (benchmarks/2026-10-13-instructions/challenger-template.jinja): reasoning_content|trim and content|trim with fixed separators '
</think>

' and '

<tool_call>'.
causes.effect:
Raw whitespace the model emits before </think> or around <tool_call> is not reproduced, so the next prompt diverges inside the cached output. Observed once in 224 Qwen3.6 continuation turns (reasoning ending '


'): 2,050 identical tokens re-processed, 17.0 s.

causes.applies_to: Templates run without preserved thinking (the Gemma-4-31B profiles used preserve_thinking=false; the Gemma-4-26B profiles used true)
causes.source: Gemma-4 template: thinking is rendered for turns after the last user message, or for tool-call turns when preserve_thinking is true. The server logs 'preserve_reasoning kwarg: not supported by template' for Gemma, so --reasoning-preserve does not apply; only the template kwarg does.
causes.effect: At a new user message the template drops earlier thoughts, so the prefix diverges right after the first prompt (LCP 138). With --ctx-checkpoints 1 the Gemma-4-31B context-v1 follow-up re-processed 9,778 tokens (512.7 s). The Gemma-4-26B runs with preserve_thinking=true lost only 97-99 mismatched tokens (1.4-3.6 s) on the same phase-2 turn, because only the final answer's thought is dropped. Qwen profiles set preserve_thinking=true and the harness returns reasoning_content, so Qwen multi-phase cases reused fully.

causes.source: server-context.cpp:3679 and :3731 (pos_min >= pos_min_thold with the threshold clamped to 0).
causes.effect: Below the window an exact prefix match still restores an older checkpoint and re-processes the previous output.

causes.source: server-task.cpp:1796 (the RAM prompt cache stores tokens, state and checkpoints and restores the best prefix match; disabled by --cache-ram 0).
causes.effect: An interleaved request replaces the only slot; returning to the earlier conversation is a full prefill. Not triggered by the sequential benchmark harness; one probable editor case (19,251 tokens, 86.2 s).

Requests that change content inside the shared prefix region, or arrive after native idle sleep (which frees the KV), are re-processed from the start. These are client and lifecycle effects; the server can only bound them with checkpoints near message boundaries.

fixes.change: Keep preserve_thinking=true / --reasoning-preserve and return reasoning_content in the trial harness for Qwen3.6 (already in place).
fixes.expected_saving: Status quo: Qwen3.6 loses 19.4 s across 224 continuation turns (0.057% of their prefill+decode time).
fixes.risk: None new. Removing it would expose Qwen multi-phase cases to the Gemma-style first-prompt divergence.

fixes.change: For Gemma-4-31B tool workflows set chat-template kwarg preserve_thinking=true, as the Gemma-4-26B profiles already do, and allow more than one checkpoint.
fixes.expected_saving: About 9.6K tokens and roughly 490 s on the one Gemma-4-31B phase-2 turn: the 26B runs with true lost 97-99 tokens on that turn, and the 16 October render probe kept 10,021 identical leading tokens instead of 137.
fixes.risk: Changes the model's input (+341 tokens in that probe) and departs from the vendor default, so results are a new configuration and must be re-scored; final-answer thoughts are still dropped.

fixes.expected_saving: Upper bound 56,155 tokens / 578 s over the four editor same-prefix events (8.3% of audited editor prefill). Only the 18 October event (170 s) had a boundary checkpoint that a larger limit would likely have kept; the others had none before the divergence. No effect expected on benchmark tool loops, whose rollbacks always target the previous prompt end.
fixes.risk: 62.8 MiB host RAM per Qwen3.6 checkpoint (16 = about 1.0 GiB, versus 0.25 GiB at 4) against a 2.5 GiB free-RAM stop guard; a smaller min-step adds checkpoint copies at more user-message starts.

fixes.expected_saving: Restores a conversation displaced by an interleaved request instead of re-prefilling it: about 86 s in the one probable case; protects against title/side requests on the single slot.
fixes.risk: Up to 2 GiB extra host RAM (a 20K-token Qwen3.6 state with checkpoints is roughly 0.5 GiB); save/restore copies cost seconds; needs a measured test before production. Does not help a same-prefix divergence.

fixes.change: Measure a build with #30557 (b11951+; the planned b12069 side build) and count forced/restored lines per audit.
fixes.expected_saving: At most the 17.0 s Qwen3.6 turn seen here; whether #30557 covers trailing newlines before </think> is untested.
fixes.risk: Separate runtime identity; launcher changes after v0.8.0 (#31417); must not replace production b11562.

fixes.change: Do not add client-side whitespace trimming to the harness.
fixes.expected_saving: None: the KV holds the model's raw tokens and the template already trims whatever the client sends, so a client cannot restore the cached form.
fixes.risk: A custom template without |trim could round-trip raw whitespace but changes prompts and frozen comparability.

fixes.expected_saving: Negligible: hybrid and iSWA losses come from recurrent/SWA state that KV shifting cannot rebuild; the attention-only models (GLM-4.7-Flash, Qwen3-Coder-30B) lost only 6.5 s and 11.1 s in total.
fixes.risk: Extra code path with no measured benefit.

fixes.change: Do not use --swa-full for Gemma-4 or Flint at 64K.
fixes.expected_saving: Would remove the short-context iSWA rollbacks (Gemma-4-26B 45 turns, 253 s; Gemma-4-31B 9 turns, 43 s; Recursive Flint 11 turns, 45 s) but not the Gemma template divergence.
fixes.risk: Full-size SWA KV: Gemma-4-26B 25 SWA layers grow from 132.8 MiB at 1,280 cells to about 6.6 GiB at 64K; Gemma-4-31B from 531 MiB to about 26.6 GiB; Flint from 27.9 MiB at 768 cells to about 2.3 GiB.

fixes.change: Choose and record a first-turn cache policy per case (cold by erasing the slot between cases, or warm).
fixes.expected_saving: Comparability rather than speed; 373.5 s of first-turn shared-prefix prefill varied across 90 cases, up to 113.5 s on Flint low-residency.
fixes.risk: Cold starts add up to a few hundred tokens per case.

fixes.change: On one public run set LLAMA_SERVER_SLOTS_DEBUG=1 and LLAMA_SERVER_SLOTS_N_DIFF=16 to print tokens around each divergence.
fixes.expected_saving: Diagnostic only: identifies the exact Gemma tool-call tail tokens and any Qwen boundary case.
fixes.risk: Prints content tokens into the log; use public fixtures only, never private audits or editor sessions.

not_established: No configuration change was tested; every saving above is an estimate from logged token counts and per-task prefill rates.
